classification.difficultyReason: Match angle markings directly, then identify quadrilateral vertices from the pair of labelled sides meeting there despite changed orientation. This directly applies the taught correspondence method.

spec.description: Paired upright isosceles triangles with two ticks on each sloping side, one tick on each base, single apex-angle arcs and double base-angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC=DE=EF; AC=DF. Apex vertices B and E correspond. Either ordering of the equal base vertices is valid.
spec.answerVisibility: Vertex names and supplied markings only; correspondence answers are hidden.

answer.short: $A\leftrightarrow D$, $B\leftrightarrow E$, $C\leftrightarrow F$. Also valid: $A\leftrightarrow F$, $B\leftrightarrow E$, $C\leftrightarrow D$.
answer.worked: The single-arc apex angles match, so $B\leftrightarrow E$. Matching the base vertices gives $A\leftrightarrow D$ and $C\leftrightarrow F$. Since both triangles are isosceles, $A\leftrightarrow F$ and $C\leftrightarrow D$ is also valid.

spec.description: Triangle STU above triangle PQR in differing orientations; retain one-, two- and three-tick sides and matching angle-arc counts.
spec.mathematics: ST corresponds to QR, TU to PR and SU to PQ. Angle S matches Q, U matches P and T matches R.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry, names and markings are visible.

answer.worked: Match the angle-arc counts: two arcs give $S\leftrightarrow Q$, one arc gives $U\leftrightarrow P$, and three arcs give $T\leftrightarrow R$. The side-tick counts agree.

spec.description: Paired differently oriented quadrilaterals with labelled interior angles and coordinate-derived right-angle squares. The right figure is a reflected and rotated copy of the left.
spec.mathematics: A and H are 54 degrees; B and E are right angles; C and F are 119 degrees; D and G are 97 degrees. Interior angles sum to 360 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Angle values and vertex labels are permanent givens; correspondences remain hidden.

answer.worked: Match equal angles: $54^\circ$ gives $A\leftrightarrow H$, $97^\circ$ gives $D\leftrightarrow G$, $119^\circ$ gives $C\leftrightarrow F$, and the right angles give $B\leftrightarrow E$.

spec.description: Paired schematic quadrilaterals with all eight supplied side-length labels, preserving source vertex positions. No units, angle marks or side ticks are added.
spec.mathematics: AB=WX=35, BC=WZ=40.3, CD=ZY=68 and DA=YX=56. Match vertices using their incident side lengths.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied lengths and names remain visible; correspondence answers are hidden.

answer.worked: Match the two side lengths meeting at each vertex: $35$ and $56$ give $A\leftrightarrow X$; $56$ and $68$ give $D\leftrightarrow Y$; $68$ and $40.3$ give $C\leftrightarrow Z$; $40.3$ and $35$ give $B\leftrightarrow W$.
